title: The Nature of the Resurrection Body
english: To improve the state of things, the Son handed [it] over to the Father, no longer reigning in the form of a slave, but as the flesh of the Word which is his own, the Son, having revealed the form of God in it. For then, the glory which he had before the world existed, which was not seized by the Son, shall be reigned by a single King, Father and Son. Therefore, it is necessary for Christ to reign for the progress of all, until all who are enemies because of sin are placed under his feet, him destroying all tyrannical authority, with which even the arch-evil, death, is destroyed, since every soul united to him that stands against death is united to the evil (1 Kor 15:27-28).

Regarding the mythology of the Greeks and to speak against deception, those saying that the parents are gods, and that he himself is said to be subject because the church is being made subject, are appropriating the persecutions and the sufferings and the subjection of the church. Those who follow Marcion, baptizing the living instead of those having died after being enlightened, do not know that baptism saves only him who has received it. But the apostle speaks of the dead as bodies for which we are baptized; for by its own word, these things do not live without a soul, but from the souls being joined to them they have life. However, even Abraham called the soulless body dead (1 Kor 15:29-30).

If the soul is not immortal, if the body is not raised, even if it is in vain to risk one's life for piety (1 Kor 15:32). As far as human reasoning reaches, I would not have endured this, desiring it for the sake of the truth, if the dead are not raised (1 Kor 15:33). Do not be deceived, O Corinthians, as if the rational soul were not perishable; for those deceiving you agree with it being destroyed, thinking so. They say that since bodies are to be squandered, they should be; for tomorrow we die, and there is no other life besides the apparent one, like the irrational animals with which the soul is associated, since it is also bound to it. Therefore, one must not endure the corrupting false discussions that destroy well-disposed minds (1 Kor 15:33-34). Watch out according to the n...

They think that they might fall into error by agreeing with the foolish regarding the resurrection. But you have indeed awakened rightly, as not all are doing this; for the wise, staying awake to do evil, unjustly awaken after having cast off the sleep of ignorance.

Regarding the one speaking in Christ who doubts about the resurrection of the dead, saying as if it were inconsistent: 'O fool, if you doubt that the dead body of a man is raised, know that what you sow, you cast into the earth dead, being convinced that it will not change into plants unless it has died as a seed' (1 Kor 15:35-40), the word about what is sown addresses one of the questions. And regarding the other question, with what kind of body they come, he gives the proof by division, and having passed through the bodies into earthly and heavenly things, he said that the glory of the rising human bodies is according to that of the heavenly sun, moon, and stars.

'Similar to the glory of the luminaries and stars, not all the bodies of those rising, but only those who have lived well and have been disciplined; for even if the bodies of the inferior are raised incorruptible, they will nevertheless be deprived of the heavenly glory' (1 Kor 15:41), it should be noted that the glory of the rising bodies is substantial, just as that of the luminaries is.

Just as the rational soul, not being virtue or vice, is receptive to both of these, so also our body, whether it becomes corruption or incorruption, receives the inherent qualities according to different times. For it is not corruption that is sown, and incorruption that is raised, but rather in incorruption. And what is sown in corruption is followed by what is sown in weakness and in dishonor and a psychic body, and similarly, what is raised in incorruption is followed by what is raised in power and in glory and a spiritual body. When we say an incorruptible body, not...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Transformation of Body and Soul
english: We speak of a fifth essence, just as some have conjectured regarding the stars, which we always say to be incorruptible; but we say incorruptible to mean that which, having come from the corruptible, is made incorruptible by the grace of God. In this way, it is to be unchanging and unalterable according to change, for such a thing has undergone [change], but it exists for the sake of enduring unto everlasting life, whether being chastened or honored (1 Kor 15:44-46).

Since the body is sown from the entanglement of the male toward the female, it is reasonable that honor and dishonor and weakness shall be about it, as it happens to be a body of a soul being corrupted in its prior quality; it stands up by the power of God, having been shown to be a spiritual body possessing incorruptibility, power, and honor, an organ of a soul, moreover not of a soul simply, but of the Holy Spirit, through the stability of a substantial change and having transitioned into spirit. Since the soul remaining in passions is such, it is reasonable that the body of such a soul is called psychic. But if the soul ascends above the passive state, it becomes spiritual, and the body of such a soul which is entwined with it is called spiritual. Since the soul, progressing, ascends toward the spiritual, he first said there would be a psychic body, then a spiritual one.

It must be understood, however, that the body of those being raised from the dead resembles the spiritual body of Christ having come to be after the resurrection. Therefore, we do not pay attention to those saying that the body stands up such as Adam had, a psychic one; for the life of the first Adam, living in a soul, prepared the man to live, but the life according to Christ is not living in a soul but is life-giving in the spirit. And the spiritual life-giving is inborn to those being raised from the dead. And he spoke fittingly, first and last, not indeed first and second man, so that we might learn that there have become some in the middle, between the first and the last man, in a state of being.

Since regarding the resurrection, theory has a depth of understanding, it is reasonable he says: Behold, I say a mystery to you (1 Kor 15:51): indeed all having died we shall sleep, but only the righteous shall be changed, having shone like...

Like the sun; for only these, changing toward the better in soul and body, will be changed. For it is not following to say in a different kind of change—such is the scripture: 'Not all shall sleep, but all shall be changed' (1 Kor 15:52-53), because of that which is immediately coming, and we also shall be changed. For if all are being changed, it is superfluous to say 'and we also shall be changed.'

The dead shall be raised from their bodies, which formerly was corruptible, having become incorruptible (1 Kor 15:52-53). But some say here that 'we shall be changed' instead of 'like others being,' regarding the dead, who, he says, are raised incorruptible in bodies, but the souls are being made better and more divine in quality. Another says that the sinners are the dead, the incorruptible ones being raised to endure eternal punishments, but those having grown vigorous in virtue are being changed from glory to glory; therefore, there is mortal and corruptible, but not again. So the corruptible puts on incorruption, and the mortal puts on immortality at the time of the resurrection of the dead (1 Kor 15:54-56).

Just as where virtue is present evil does not exist, so where immortality is present death is made to vanish (1 Kor 15:54). Therefore, the mortal having put on immortality, death having been defeated is swallowed up (1 Kor 15:54), as it is said to him: 'Where is your victory, with which conquering you made dead? Where is your sting, with which pricking, you were strong?' (1 Kor 15:55-56). For it stings by entering into the thoughts, casting sin into those struck by it, but it conquers those sinning in practice. The usage lies in Hosea, not in the very words; for instead of 'the justice of' your [God], the apostle said 'victory' (1 Kor 15:57).

Since the enemy death has been released, you stand faithfully and firmly, working continually and without division the work set before you by the Lord (1 Kor 15:58), undauntedly emboldened, as the labor of you in the Lord is not in vain, an eternal reward lying in store for those who always do the work (1 Kor 15:58). On the first of the Saturdays, the resurrection day of the Lord, you treasure up (1 Kor 16:2)...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Steadfastness and the Marks of True Piety
english: Therefore, if your power is able to set aside [the delay] by itself and without necessity, so that I may find you ready for the gift when I arrive, so that after my arrival, things for fellowship may become well-disposed. In Ephesus, therefore, he wrote this letter to the Corinthians. And he says there to remain for a reasonable cause; for a door, surpassing all and being very active toward the hearers, has been opened to him; from which he had many opposing demons, liars, and sorcerers and deceivers; for the evil ones become many in opposing, when they see the word of faith prevailing among those receiving it; and it is his custom to call the door of the boldness of the word of piety (1 Kor 16:8-9).

When those being instructed are firm and immovable concerning piety, the teachers arrive to them without fear, not having received that some laziness might exist among the hearers. Therefore he says: take care of yourselves, so that Timothy may dare to come to you, not being afraid, lest you be turned away (1 Kor 16:10-11). By this being indicated, he persisted in the fearing, and in the sixth letter he said: I fear lest, just as the serpent deceived Eve in his craftiness, so your thoughts might be corrupted. For this Timothy, about whom I write the following things, is a genuine servant of God, working the work of the master similarly to me. Therefore let him not be treated lightly among you, but let him be received with genuineness and with love, and also let him be sent forward; for I am waiting in Asia until he returns to me with the brothers.

Since Apollos was a bishop of Corinth, he departed from them because of the schisms among them, and he was with Paul, and now having been invited, he did not stay with the letter; and he says the cause for which he did not depart: that it was not the will (1 Kor 16:12). Then, cheering them up, he writes; and he will come when he has opportunity, providing the opportunity of his stay with you, when there are no longer schisms among you (1 Kor 16:13). It follows that which is due to one properly watching in the not [being]...

Give sleep to the eyes and no lingering to the eyelids, to stand firmly in faith, which is followed by becoming manly and being strengthened as a soldier and athlete of Christ, who does all things with love toward God and neighbor (1 Cor 16:14-16).

They are called firstfruits either because they believed before others, or because they excel in piety, or because they are prominent in lineage; these, because of the humility existing in them, were not ordained, but being led by their own intention toward this, they set themselves to service. Therefore subject yourselves to such, having them as an icon and a pattern, so that you too may set yourselves to the service of the saints (1 Cor 16:14-16).

Along with Stephanos, Fortunatus and Achaios fulfilled what was lacking to you, being of that same intention as he, and they refreshed your spirit and mine (1 Cor 16:17-18). But the Spirit refreshes him who thinks and does the things of piety; for the Spirit seeks the good things of being; regarding faults, it is called soul, but regarding the saints, it is called Spirit, which surpasses by desiring the beautiful. Therefore, those living piously and thinking piously must be recognized as thinking and doing the same. Thus also Origen glorifies the Spirit as having more than the soul in virtue, even if it is Spirit and the soul.
He writes that the churches of Asia greet you, and all the holy and pious men dwelling in it, sufficiently rousing them toward love (1 Cor 16:19).

Lest they be deceived by some writing from outside the apostle's designation, this sign is made: that he has engraved it with his own hand, but that which is written is with his holy right hand (1 Cor 16:21). If anyone does not love our Lord, let him be anathema. Maranatha. But he who does not love the Lord does not keep his commandments; therefore also anathema is he who, knowing that the Lord came who judges the works of men, says: 'I love those who love me.' But if he loves those who love him, what will he find to scrutinize among those who do not love?
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
